model_requests.question: erase vs a scheduled FHIR sync task
model_requests.model_hint: as-built: EraseGraph keeps the fhir_graphs row and task, sets wm_rsrc=wm_ver=0 and interp NULL (Eraser.cls:180-183,1151-1180); the next task tick (SyncOnce) re-projects the whole repository, so erased content is live again and a following redaction is refused (target_live). reviewed (decisions.md HD-1502): transient erase may refill; durable removal = unschedule (verified paused) + erase, and the invariant 'after durable removal no content of G is live until an explicit re-register' holds. Negative control: durable removal without unschedule must be caught. Include F-C1501 (orphan task after a failed Schedule bookkeeping) as an as-built variant.

model_requests.question: erase during a running sync
model_requests.model_hint: as-built: SyncOnce reads watermarks in Open() BEFORE taking Lock +^IVG.FHIRGraph(g):0 (FHIRGraph.cls:550-556, 1736-1737); each RunBatch commits its rows together with an ABSOLUTE UPDATE fhir_graphs SET wm=? (FHIRGraph.cls:1966-1968); EraseGraph takes no lock and resets wm to 0 in its own transaction. Interleaving batch_k commit < erase commit < batch_k+1 commit leaves G holding only batch k+1 rows with wm past rows it lacks, until a rebuild. Invariant: whenever no txn is open, every live repository key with ID <= wm has its node in G. reviewed: erase takes the sync lock (busy or wait) or the batch's watermark write is compare-and-set against the value read under the lock.

model_requests.question: one unreadable resource and sync progress
model_requests.model_hint: as-built: a poison key makes ResyncKey throw (FHIRGraph.cls:2380-2397, 2976-2988); the batch and its watermark roll back together; every later sync fails on the same batch (last_error names it). Properties: safety 'wm never passes an unapplied key' holds; progress AG EF(wm = max) fails while the poison stays and holds once a 'repair' action exists (working assumption: fail, name the key, document recovery). Alternative quarantine design: progress unconditional, with invariant 'every skipped key is recorded'; negative control: a skip that advances wm without recording must be caught.
